dimension: Reproduction harness and documentation (thesis_expected_values.yaml, thesis_assertions.py, _build_reproduction_notebook.py, REGENERATE.md, glossary/README/coverage docs, X-ray control notebook)
summary: The harness currently runs 1,364 checks (I executed thesis_assertions.run_all read-only: 1364 results, 0 failures), not the 194 in the brief nor the 257 in README.md:15/67; the registry has 60 stages (REGENERATE.md:17, :103-115, and the builder's loops), not 58. Roughly 850 of the 1,364 result rows sit on a crystal-referenced column (rmsd, bestfit_rmsd, centroid_dist, crystal contacts) and move under nearest-copy: every cell of Tables 2, 3, 6, 8, 18, 19 (rates/wins), 21, 25, 26, 27, the near/form/triple columns of Table 1 (90 of 130 cells), the near-native half of Table 24, the near/both rows of Table 20 (24 of 36), Table 4's rates, the whole Appendix H.9 block, the refiner contrasts, the Figure 39 and audit prose, and 14 of the 39 figure md5 pairs (image3-9, 11, 24, 25, 44-47). Unchanged: cohort, determinism, Tables 5, 9, 10 (values), 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, Orai prose (fig 23/24), Table 1's poses/valid columns, Table 24's all-poses half, Table 20's validity rows, image2 and every Orai/dataset figure. Where the six-arm all-depths CSV covers an arm I derived the new value (Tables 1 near columns for 6 arms, 2, 6 complexes/poses_near2, 8 exh128 rows, 18 for 5 of 7 variants, 19 for 2 of 4 contrasts, 21 rates/wins for 2 of 4, 22, 24 near-pose counts, 25, 26 RMSD half, H.9 in full); everything on bestfit/Kabsch, crystal clusters, crystal contacts, the filmstrip, Holm p-values and the arms not in the CSV is "recompute". Notable derived consequences: Appendix H.9's rank-1 TOST verdict flips (equivalent_within_10pp true -> false, 90% CI upper bound 11.7), MDE 9.8 -> 10.5 pp, discordant 112 -> 129, n_needed 4200 -> 1100, power 0.12 -> 0.32; the validity-gate cost ("two at rank-1, four at top-5, three deeper") is unchanged; Table 22's AutoDock-gnina, EquiBind-gnina and raw-AutoDock rows coincide numerically with the old values. In thesis_assertions.py only seven gate lines hard-code the column (:122-124, :393, :426, :611, :615, :1432, :1457) plus thesis_endpoint_diagnostics.py:77 behind check_table_25/26/H.9; the other check_* functions read regenerated sidecars and need no code change. If the hub writes the nearest-copy value into the existing rmsd/pb_rmsd/pb_kabsch_rmsd/bestfit_rmsd/centroid_dist/contact_recovery/plif_recovery columns and adds *_ref_instance secondary columns, no consumer changes and adding rmsd_ref_instance to _CACHE_REQUIRED_COLS (hub :13187-13191) makes every stale per_pose cache unusable even under --reuse-cache. Fourteen of the 19 section-3 stages must re-run in dependency order behind bench_pose_comparison; bench_figure1, bench_pandamap, all PoseBusters, docking, Orai and dataset stages do not. A new cheap stage (reference-convention contrast from per_pose_metrics, the inverted form of the M2 doc's proposed bench_nearest_copy_sensitivity) plus a yaml block is needed or the M2 quantification lives nowhere in the harness. REGENERATE.md is generated (:3) and must not be hand-edited; the X-ray control notebook busts the deposited ligand with no reference and no RMSD (builder :283, :503) and is convention-independent.

decisions.question: How should the hub expose the nearest-copy values to the harness and its 14 downstream consumers?
options: A: write nearest-copy into the existing columns rmsd, pb_rmsd, pb_kabsch_rmsd, pb_rmsd_within_2A, bestfit_rmsd, centroid_dist, contact_recovery, plif_recovery and add *_ref_instance secondary columns plus n_copies, nearest_copy_idx, nearest_copy_is_ref; add rmsd_ref_instance to _CACHE_REQUIRED_COLS

B: add rmsd_nearest_copy etc. as new columns and rename the column in thesis_assertions.py (:122-124, :393, :426, :611, :615, :1432, :1457), thesis_endpoint_diagnostics.py:77, the yaml table_26.metrics and 11 consumer scripts
decisions.recommendation: A. It leaves thesis_assertions.py and every consumer untouched, the single-instance value survives as the secondary column the brief requires, and the extra required cache column turns the --reuse-cache trap into a hard refusal of any pre-switch per_pose_metrics.csv.

decisions.question: Does the reference-convention contrast get a harness stage and yaml block?
options: Register bench_reference_convention (section 3, BITEXACT, CHEAP, needs bench_pose_comparison) writing reference_convention_contrast.csv from rmsd and rmsd_ref_instance, plus a table_28 yaml block asserting multi_copy_ids 143, multi_copy_analysed 138, rank-1 gains 38/29/2, top-15 gains 15/12/3 and a zero-loss count
Leave the M2 quantification to prose and the probe directory only
decisions.recommendation: Register it. Without a stage and a table_* key the M2 effect appears in neither REGENERATE.md's table index (regenerate_guide.py:323 lists only table_* keys) nor the assertion run, and the probe under nearest_copy_probe/ is not wired to the registry.

decisions.question: Do the crystal-contact metrics (Table 4, Figure 7 Jaccard, Figure 39, the audit's site filter, contact_recovery/plif_recovery) follow the nearest copy?
options: Yes: compute a PandaMap fingerprint for every copy in <ID>_ligands.sdf and pick per pose the copy nearest by rmsd (pandamap_interaction_report.py:599 and the hub's contact metrics)
No: keep the interaction family single-instance and state the exemption in the yaml table_4 comment, the Methods and the audit
decisions.recommendation: Yes, because the brief defines the convention as every crystal-referenced metric and a mixed convention would put Table 4's n on PB-valid poses that recovered a copy while scoring their contacts against a different chain. Cost is the largest of the switch (new fingerprinting of 138 complexes' alternate copies) and it is the item to schedule first.

decisions.question: Which copy defines the crystal cluster in pose_cluster_crystal_pocket_report.py (Table 3, Figures 5, 6, 38)?
options: Per pose: a pose's cluster is crystal-compatible if within the radius of any copy
Per complex: the copy nearest to the most poses, or the reference copy only
decisions.recommendation: Per pose (any copy), consistent with the per-pose minimum used for rmsd; document the rule in the stage notes and the yaml table_3 comment.

decisions.question: How are the dated documents handled?
options: Edit REPRODUCTION_COVERAGE_2026-09-03.md and DEFENCE_NOTES_NUMBER_GLOSSARY.md in place
Write REPRODUCTION_COVERAGE_<date>.md and a new glossary version, leave the dated files as records
decisions.recommendation: New dated files, per the house rule that deliverables are revised as new versions; REGENERATE.md is regenerated, never edited; README.md, thesis_latex/README.md and THESIS_REPRODUCTION.md are living documents and are edited.

decisions.question: In what order are the yaml values re-transcribed?
options: Copy the regenerated sidecar values into the yaml directly
Rebuild the thesis tables from the regenerated outputs first, then transcribe the printed values into the yaml, then run the harness
decisions.recommendation: The second. The yaml records what the thesis prints (yaml :2-12); transcribing from the outputs makes the harness a tautology and hides a table left un-updated, which is exactly how Table 21 drifted.

open_questions: Should bestfit_rmsd/pb_kabsch_rmsd be evaluated against the copy selected by in-place RMSD (PoseBusters choose_by="rmsd" behaviour, rmsd.py:41, :61) or minimised independently over copies? The former is what 'derived from that nearest copy' implies and what the installed check_rmsd does by default.

Table 4's n cells (15) are expected unchanged because they count PB-valid poses at rank, but a PandaMap fingerprint may be unavailable for some alternate copies on other chains; verify after the re-run rather than assume.

Appendix H.9's rank-1 TOST verdict flips (equivalent_within_10pp true -> false; 90 % CI upper bound 11.7) and the power narrative changes (MDE 9.8 -> 10.5 pp, power 0.12 -> 0.32, n_needed 4,200 -> 1,100). Which body sentences depend on 'only rank-1 is equivalent within 10 points' and 'roughly 4,200' belongs to the thesis-text dimension.

The metal stratum (78 of 303 complexes with a metal within 5 A of the crystal ligand, glossary :647-654) is defined against the reference instance; whether it should be recomputed against any copy is undecided.

The hub's full re-score runtime under nearest-copy is unmeasured; the probe scored 53,651 poses against all copies in about one minute on 16 cores with symmetry_rmsd only, the hub additionally computes PoseBusters RMSD, strain and contacts for 241,914 rows, so bench_pose_comparison stays MODERATE but should be timed.

Three counts disagree: the brief says 58 stages and 194 asserted numbers, README.md:15-16 and :67 say 60 stages and 257 numbers, REGENERATE.md:17 says 60 stages, REPRODUCTION_COVERAGE:26 says 1,362 assertions, and the harness returned 1,364 results today. The registry has 60 (builder loops at :255, :275, :623, :844, :858, :927). Which figure the thesis itself prints, if any, was not found in body_appendix_short.tex.
